title: W2 and Walsh close by GQR eligible circles and affine completions

theorem.statement: For every odd prime p, the binary incidence words of nonsquare Miquelian circles meeting {infinity,0} in 0 or 2 points span H0 intersect ker(e_infinity+e_0), of dimension (p^2-1)/2.
proof_route: A same-type tangent pencil sums to the all-ones word.
A tangent pencil with exactly two edge-incompatible circles identifies their classes modulo the eligible-circle span.
The bipartite tangency graph is a Cayley graph on M=(F_{p^2}^*)^2 with connection set {(1+r sigma)^(-2): r in F_p}.
If the connection set failed to generate M, a nontrivial even character eta of F_(p^2)^* would equal one on an affine F_p-line.

Parameterising that line by the norm-one torus converts its character sum to Katz's t=-2 Soto-Andrade sum. The two exceptional character pairs both induce trivial eta, so the 2 sqrt(p) bound applies and contradicts a sum of p for p>=5; p=3 is direct.
All edge-incompatible circle generators therefore have one quotient class, which cancels in every edge-even codeword.

circle_completion.criterion: A Max-minus vector y can be flipped on a nonsquare circle S and remain Max-minus iff y restricted to S equals plus or minus the unique signed sparse -p eigenvector v_S.

affine_completion_close.theorem: For every T subset F_p of size (p+1)/2, h_T(infinity)=1 and h_T(a+b omega)=+1 iff b is in T satisfies C h_T=p h_T. If 0 is in T, nonsquare dilation and the infinity sign switch give a completion of the standard nonsquare circle.
affine_completion_close.pair_prescription: For an outside pair sigma*u,sigma*v with nonzero transverse coordinates b,d, choose T containing zero so s_T(b)s_T(d)=chi(u-v). If b=d the target is automatically +1; otherwise prescribe equal membership for +1 and opposite membership for -1, then extend T to size (p+1)/2.
affine_completion_close.consequence: Every eligible nonsquare circle is the binary difference of two Max-minus points in U. Together with the eligible-circle span theorem, dir(U)=H0 intersect ker(e_infinity+e_0), closing W1, W2, and Walsh 15.406 E for every odd prime.

oeis_web.note: Earlier matches were unrelated numerical coincidences; the two post-close exact count queries returned null. Crossref exact-object searches for Paley affine-halfspace eigenvectors and edge-even Miquelian-circle codes found no direct prior statement. This is not a novelty claim.

backend: Exact affine construction and pair exhaustions on soulkiller; full p=11 data-local holdout plus superseded p=19 HiGHS/CP-SAT attempts on NUKA; no process left running.
note: The eligible-circle span plus explicit affine completions prove W1, W2, and Walsh 15.406 E for every odd prime. Unrelated 5+-level and other E1 leftovers remain open.
